triggers.grounds: Re-derived from bytes and well calibrated. The row quotes the whole of MT 5:8, וְיִתְר֥וֹן אֶ֖רֶץ בַּכֹּ֣ל היא ה֑וּא מֶ֥לֶךְ לְשָׂדֶ֖ה נֶעֱבָֽד, and that run collates byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.8; the ketiv/qere description is exact -- the inline unpointed ketiv היא stands immediately before the pointed qere ה֑וּא on the third-person pronoun, and MT 5:8 is one of the twelve K/Q verses in the pmarks inventory (four of them inside the offset zone). The seam is sound at any band: the word-bound content-token intersection (skeleton tier) with BOTH neighbours is empty -- MT 5:7 x MT 5:8 = 0 tokens and MT 5:8 x MT 5:9 = 0 tokens -- so the stated topic-isolation warrant is byte-true rather than thematic assertion, and all three dual refs are arithmetically right (web:Eccl.5.9 = oshb:Eccl.5.8; citation_sweep.py over a private copy of the six rows returns status GREEN, zero problems). The stated reason for the low band is honest and strategy-conformant: the construction is a live construal crux the row explicitly declines to adjudicate, and MT 5:8-9 is one of the regions the book strategy pre-registers as expected-low-confidence (difficult syntax plus K/Q). WEB's rendering is cited descriptively and carries no boundary or rival-rejection weight, so no tier-4 driver stands in the row. If anything the band is conservative -- the two empty seam intersections would support a higher one -- but a conservative band over sound byte grounds is not a defect.

All eleven Hebrew runs in the row collate byte tier at their cited MT refs (batch collate: byte for every run, status GREEN). The two mark claims are exact: the refrain tag גַּם זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל is genuinely verse-final at MT 5:9 (its last three tokens), and MT 5:10 carries the inline unpointed ketiv ראית immediately before the pointed qere רְא֥וּת, with both MT 5:10 and MT 5:8 standing in the twelve-verse K/Q inventory and both correctly labelled offset-zone. The front-seam claim of no shared vocabulary with the monarchy crux re-derives TRUE (MT 5:8 x MT 5:9 word-bound skeleton intersection = 0 tokens); at the rear seam MT 5:10 x MT 5:11 share only the function word אִם, and the row discloses on its own initiative the two content roots that do straddle it, יֹאכֵ֑ל and וְהַשָּׂבָע֙ at MT 5:11. Its single digit is right AND names its numbering space, which is this book's specific hazard: hevel-family verses in MT chapter 5 = 2 (MT 5:6 and MT 5:9), and this row carries MT 5:9. The stated reason for medium_low -- compressed clauses in the opening verse plus the second verse's own K/Q -- is honest, and the WEB ch-5 offset zone is a pre-registered expected-low-confidence region. A well-calibrated low-band row with sound grounds.

All three matched phrases stand in the shipped fields and each violates the register law (row prose describes the TEXT; cross-row references are verse-anchored): 'a condition the next row's opening case will negate with the same verb' (boundary_rationale), 'is carried forward into the next row, across this row's own rear seam' (device_notes) and 'completing the disclosure the preceding row began' (device_notes). Two carry an argumentative cross-row claim, so they were re-derived from bytes and are TRUE: MT 5:18's וְהִשְׁלִיט֨וֹ (hiphil of the sh-l-t root, byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.18) is negated at MT 6:2 by וְלֹֽא יַשְׁלִיטֶ֤נּוּ (byte tier at oshb:Eccl.6.2) governing the same eat-of-it complement, so the same-verb antithesis holds. The third is pure process narration about another row's disclosure act and carries no textual content (the paseq seg at MT 5:17 is indeed disclosed by the preceding row as well). True claims phrased in workflow register plus one bare process reference = confirmed register defect at low severity; no evidence defect.

findings.claim: Three positional row references stand in the row's prose where the register law requires verse-anchored cross-row reference.
findings.grounds: Present verbatim in the shipped row: 'the next row's opening case will negate with the same verb' (boundary_rationale), 'carried forward into the next row' (device_notes), 'completing the disclosure the preceding row began' (device_notes). The byte claims behind the first two are true -- MT 5:18 וְהִשְׁלִיט֨וֹ against MT 6:2 וְלֹֽא יַשְׁלִיטֶ֤נּוּ, both byte tier at their cited refs -- so the defect is register, not evidence; the third has no textual content and is workflow narration outright.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (no span effect): verse-anchor the two argumentative references (e.g. 'the case at web:Eccl.6.1-Eccl.6.2 negates the same hiphil') and delete 'completing the disclosure the preceding row began'.

findings.claim: The device_notes Hebrew quote binds to K/Q verse MT 5:17 with no ketiv/qere disclosure in that field.
findings.grounds: citation_sweep.py over a private copy of the six rows returns status GREEN with two prose_dual_warns, both reading 'M8-Eccl-031: Hebrew quote in row.device_notes binds to K/Q verse oshb:Eccl.5.17 with no ketiv/qere disclosure in-field'. The quoted run תַּֽחַת הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ collates byte tier at oshb:Eccl.5.17 and does not itself cross the note -- the K/Q sits later in that verse, unpointed ketiv חיו before pointed qere חַיָּ֛יו -- and the row does disclose that note correctly in boundary_rationale, so this is a per-field disclosure shortfall, not an evidence defect. The row's other mark work is sound: the paseq seg at MT 5:17 is in the eleven-seg inventory and is cited single-witness and count-only with no position claim, and check_marks.py returns GREEN with zero flags.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (no span effect): carry the standing single-witness K/Q disclosure into device_notes alongside the MT 5:17 run.

triggers.grounds: The medium_low hold is well calibrated and the reason it states is byte-true. The cluster's declared driver re-derives exactly: a word-bound skeleton sweep of the mourning word returns 2 verses book-wide, MT 7:2 בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל and MT 7:4 בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל, both inside the span, and the contiguous-substring sweep returns the same 2 verses, so no prefixed or suffixed form escapes it -- the book-exclusivity claim is true on both sweep modes. It matches neither excluded neighbour at any tier (collating the MT 7:2 form against oshb:Eccl.7.1 and against oshb:Eccl.7.5 returns tier 'none' both times). Tier discipline is honest and if anything conservative: the bracket phrase collates byte tier at MT 7:2 and only skeleton tier at MT 7:4 exactly as the row states, while the bare mourning word actually collates accent_stripped across the two ends -- a tier ABOVE the skeleton identity claimed. The 'thin but real' internal chain is exact: MT 7:2 x MT 7:3 share exactly one word-bound content token (ט֞וֹב / ט֥וֹב) and MT 7:3 x MT 7:4 exactly one (לֵֽב / לֵ֤ב). The rival's rejection ground also re-derives TRUE: the MT 7:5 x MT 7:6 word-bound content-token intersection is empty. Both cross-seam devices are disclosed rather than suppressed -- the fools word that does straddle the rear seam into MT 7:5 (word-bound sweep: 3 verses book-wide, MT 7:4, MT 7:5, MT 7:9, exactly as cited) and the tov-opener anaphora at the front seam (inventory: 12 book-wide, 7 in ch 7, as cited). Thin cohesion honestly held is what medium_low is for; the count-object defect recorded below does not touch either seam.

findings.claim: The rival is characterised as the laughter ROOT with a book-wide digit of 2 verses, but that digit holds only for the defective spelling; the root stands in 5 verses book-wide across two attested spellings.
findings.grounds: The row writes 'the laughter root, מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק (oshb:Eccl.7.3) / שְׂחֹ֣ק (oshb:Eccl.7.6) (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6)'. A contiguous skeleton sweep of the defective spelling does return exactly those 2 verses, but the plene spelling with the mater vav escapes it: a skeleton sweep of the plene form returns 3 further verses -- MT 2:2 לִשְׂח֖וֹק, MT 3:4 לִשְׂח֔וֹק, MT 10:19 לִשְׂחוֹק֙ -- so the object the sentence NAMES occurs in 5 verses book-wide, not 2. This is the mater-lectionis hazard the book's own hazard catalog names (sweep per attested spelling; for a root-level claim sweep each spelling and say so) together with the count-object rule (name the object -- spelling vs root -- then count). It is not load-bearing: the rival is rejected on the token-empty MT 7:5 x MT 7:6 seam (re-derived: intersection empty) and on the mourning word's verified book-exclusivity, and the correction weakens the rival rather than the row, so no seam moves. check_universals.py does not catch it because the claim does carry a digit (11 claims seen, 0 flags).
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (no span effect): name the swept object as the spelling -- e.g. 'the defective laughter spelling (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6; the plene spelling adds 3 further verses book-wide)' -- or restate the digit as the root's true 5-verse book-wide count.

findings.claim: The opening Hebrew splice begins mid-clause while the curly-quoted WEB run paired with it renders the whole comparative clause, so gloss extent exceeds splice extent.
findings.grounds: The splice בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל מִלֶּ֨כֶת֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה is tokens 4-9 of MT 7:2 and collates byte tier at oshb:Eccl.7.2; the WEB run paired with it, “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting” (web:Eccl.7.2), is verbatim (check_web_quotes.py: 16 quotes checked, 0 flags) but additionally renders the three tokens the splice omits, ט֞וֹב לָלֶ֣כֶת אֶל. Mechanical only -- the same field's other pairing quotes MT 7:4 in full against the full WEB verse with exact parity, and no boundary claim rests on the overhang.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (no span effect): open the splice at the verse's first token so the extents match, or trim the WEB run to the clause the splice actually covers.

triggers.grounds: medium_low is right, and the re-derivation shows the row is MORE exposed than its prose admits, which supports the band rather than undercutting it. Both verses are quoted in full and collate byte tier at oshb:Eccl.7.11 and oshb:Eccl.7.12. But the pair's word-bound content-token intersection is EMPTY at skeleton tier: the two wisdom tokens differ by the definite article, חָכְמָ֖ה at MT 7:11 against הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה at MT 7:12, and cross-collation returns tier 'none' in both directions. The cluster therefore clears the byte-grounded-cohesion bar only on a root match across two different attested forms plus the syntactic dependency of MT 7:12's opening כִּ֛י -- and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so that dependency is a form claim no tool can settle. The cross-seam disclosure is byte-true and correctly refused as binding: MT 7:10's own שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל זֶֽה collates byte tier at oshb:Eccl.7.10, and both tokens the row says MT 7:12 repeats collate byte tier at oshb:Eccl.7.12. Its single digit re-derives true (MT 7:11 is the 6th of the 7 in-chapter tov-opener sites among 12 book-wide, and its opening token is the non-bare tovah form as stated). A contested cluster call inside an owner-ruled atomic-default zone, resting on a construction run no tool can verify, is exactly what medium_low should carry.

findings.claim: device_notes carries a positional row reference where the register law requires a verse anchor.
findings.grounds: The shipped device_notes reads 'shares the ראה root with the following row's own opening imperative'. The byte claim behind it is TRUE -- לְרֹאֵ֥י at MT 7:11 and רְאֵ֖ה at MT 7:13 both collate byte tier at their cited refs and share the same three-consonant skeleton -- so the defect is register only. The slice carries this lane's evidence for the row although its trigger tag list carries only the confidence tag, so it is recorded here as a finding rather than as a trigger disposition.

findings.claim: The saying_cluster's cohesion is asserted at root level without disclosing that the pair shares no word-bound content token, which is the very test the sibling atomic decision in the same sentence zone applies.
findings.grounds: Re-derived: the MT 7:11 x MT 7:12 word-bound skeleton intersection is EMPTY; the wisdom tokens differ by the definite article (חָכְמָ֖ה / הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה) and collate 'none' against each other's verses. The row states only that both verses share the wisdom root as their argument's subject, writing that root bare, unpointed and with no tier label, while the neighbouring single_saying decision at web:Eccl.7.5 rejects clustering precisely because 'the pair's word-bound content-token intersection is empty and no construction run replaces it'. The two decisions are reconcilable -- this row does supply a construction run -- but the row never says the token test fails here, so a reader cannot see which limb of the cluster bar carries the weight, and the strategy makes pointed splices plus tier labels mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only (no span effect): quote the two attested forms with their tiers, state that the pair's word-bound content-token intersection is empty, and rest the cluster explicitly on the construction run.

triggers.grounds: Conservative but defensible, so not a defect. The byte case is the strongest of any adjacent pair in this stretch and every claim re-derives: MT 7:13 x MT 7:14 share THREE word-bound tokens at skeleton tier -- אֶת, הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים / הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים, and רְאֵ֖ה / רְאֵ֑ה -- against function-word-only intersections at both seams (MT 7:12 x MT 7:13 = כִּ֛י / כִּ֣י; MT 7:14 x MT 7:15 = אֶת). The digit is exact: the definite ha-elohim inventory lists 28 verses book-wide and MT 7:13 and MT 7:14 are consecutive entries in it. All twelve Hebrew runs collate byte tier at their cited refs, the two curly-quoted WEB runs are verbatim with in-field web: refs and have exact extent parity with their splices, and both cross-seam continuities are disclosed and byte-true -- רָאִ֖יתִי at MT 7:15, and the resh-ayin pair רָעָ֖ה against בְּרָעָתֽוֹ explicitly held as a different object, not blended. The honest residual the band should carry is the one the row itself discloses: admonition_unit deviates from the owner-ruled single_saying default of the 7:1-14 sentence zone, and each verse would stand as a complete saying alone. No reason for the band is written into any row field, but the strategy assigns the why_low_confidence text to the sidecar layer, which lies outside this audit's evidence scope, so no defect is recorded for that omission.
